processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting; casting into cylindrical copper moulds
processing_steps.cooling_medium: cylindrical copper moulds (32 mm diameter × 186 mm length)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: No further heat treatment reported; as-cast terminal state.
All samples cut in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); specimen surfaces ground.

structures.overall_structure: As-cast dendritic microstructure: Fe-Al matrix (A2 bcc disordered) with TaC precipitates (fibrous, lamellar in eutectic); matrix dendrites equiaxed and columnar (30 μm and 30×80 μm).

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: dendrites: equiaxed 30 μm and columnar 30×80 μm; no polygonal grains reported ('-' in grains column)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: compression specimens (6×6×10) mm³; tensile specimens 3.5×5 mm² cross-section with 15 mm gauge length
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: samples cut in the direction of the longitudinal axis of the ingot (casting direction); surfaces ground; ZWICK 1474 universal testing machine

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Room-temperature compression (Fig. 2a, curve 5): steepest parabolic hardening, terminating just below the 1400 MPa gridline. Room-temperature tension (Fig. 3a, curve 5): linear elastic loading followed by abrupt vertical load drop at ~700 MPa (fracture with negligible elongation).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: samples held 30 min at testing temperature before loading

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: deformation rate 10^-4 s^-1; elevated-temperature tests in protective argon atmosphere; samples held 30 min at testing temperature before loading
characterization_methods.purpose: determine yield stress in compression/tension, ductility, and elevated-temperature strength
characterization_methods.key_findings: Room-temperature compressive yield stress 868 MPa; brittle in tension (no yield stress or elongation reported); tension-compression asymmetry at room and elevated temperatures; compressive yield stress decreases monotonically with temperature.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SEM-Hitachi S-530, 20 kV, working distance 15 mm, secondary electrons (SE)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: secondary electrons (SE); 20 kV; working distance 15 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: investigate fracture surfaces of ruptured tensile specimens
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets (fracture mode TGC).

unmapped_findings: Fracture mode at room temperature: transgranular cleavage (TGC); SEM (Fig. 4e) shows coarse transgranular cleavage facets (Table 2, Fig. 4e).

Room-temperature tensile test: no yield stress or total elongation reported ('-' in Table 2); Fig. 3a curve 5 shows linear elastic loading then abrupt vertical load drop at ~700 MPa, i.e. brittle fracture with negligible elongation.
Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C has higher compressive yield stress (868 MPa) but lower matrix hardness (291 HB) than Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (827 MPa, 309 HB) (Table 2, b0023).
Tension-compression asymmetry: compressive yield stress exceeds tensile yield stress at room temperature and at 650/800 °C (b0040, Figs 7 and 8).

Elevated-temperature compressive yield stress decreases monotonically with increasing temperature (no yield stress anomaly); steep drop between ~600 and 800 °C, converging to 0–100 MPa at 800 °C (Fig. 5).
